executive_summary: The shop's microservice architecture shows a critical weakness: small delays in several services instantly break all major user journeys, indicating a wide blast radius. The cart service and its valkey-cart cache act as single points of failure, collapsing the cart journey when they crash. Hidden coupling between astronomy-db and checkout further exposes undocumented dependencies. Finally, three core services have extremely low resilience scores, making them fragile under load. Addressing these issues - adding redundancy, isolating dependencies, and improving the weakest services - will raise

weaknesses.title: Wide blast radius across core journeys
weaknesses.explanation: A small latency injection on any of these services aborts the whole set of user journeys (cart, checkout, home, product). The map predicts the same four journeys, showing that failures propagate far beyond the affected component.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-141542-f9bb, exp-143142-3011, exp-164224-dcfe, exp-201645-55d7 all have impact 1.00, breadth 1.00, degrading cart,checkout,home,product.

fix.fix_title: Add circuit breaker and timeout in frontend-proxy
fix.steps: Add a circuit-breaker library (e.g., opossum) to the frontend-proxy. Wrap each outbound HTTP call to astronomy-db, product-catalog and valkey-cart with a breaker configured to open after 3 consecutive >80 ms latencies, a 30 s cool-down, and a fallback that returns a cached response or a graceful error page. Also set a per-request timeout of 200 ms so delayed calls are aborted before they cascade.
fix.expected_effect: Latency spikes no longer abort all journeys; calls that exceed the timeout are short-circuited, limiting impact to the affected endpoint.

weaknesses.title: Cart service is a single point of failure
weaknesses.explanation: When the cart service crashes the cart journey fails completely while other journeys remain unaffected, indicating no redundancy for the core cart functionality.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-142250-d200 crash on cart aborts cart journey, impact 1.00, breadth 0.25, only cart degraded.

fix.fix_title: Restart policy and healthcheck for cart service
fix.steps: Add a restart policy and healthcheck to the cart service and limit its memory to 512 MiB. The healthcheck polls /health every 15 s; if it fails 3 times Docker restarts the container. This ensures the cart service recovers automatically after a crash.
fix.compose_override:
services:
  cart:
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test:
      - CMD
      - curl
      - -f
      - http://localhost:8080/health
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512M
fix.expected_effect: Cart container is automatically restarted on crash and stays within memory limits, reducing downtime to seconds and keeping cart journey available.

weaknesses.applicability: Auto-applicable with `faultline fix` (cart: restart unless-stopped, memory 512 MB); propose-only part: healthcheck.

weaknesses.title: Valkey-cart cache is a single point of failure
weaknesses.explanation: A crash of the valkey-cart cache stops the cart journey, showing the cart flow depends entirely on this cache with no fallback.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-104221-fd4f crash on valkey-cart aborts cart, impact 1.00, breadth 0.25, only cart degraded.

fix.fix_title: Add Valkey replica with Sentinel failover
fix.steps: Deploy a second valkey-cart instance and run a Valkey Sentinel container to provide automatic failover. Update the cart client configuration to point to the sentinel address so reads/writes are redirected to the surviving node if one crashes. This removes the single point of failure.
fix.expected_effect: If one valkey-cart node crashes, Sentinel promotes the replica and the cart service continues without interruption.

weaknesses.title: Hidden dependencies cause unexpected checkout degradation
weaknesses.explanation: A tiny 50 ms delay on astronomy-db triggers a safety-agent alert for checkout latency, even though checkout is outside the predicted blast radius, revealing undocumented coupling.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-165933-0066 delay 50 ms on astronomy-db shows checkout p95 285 ms > baseline 74 ms, yet checkout degraded.

fix.fix_title: Timeout and cache fallback for astronomy-db calls in checkout
fix.steps: In the checkout service, wrap calls to astronomy-db with a timeout of 100 ms and a circuit-breaker that falls back to a read-through cache populated on successful calls. If the DB is delayed, the request returns cached data and the checkout latency stays within SLA.
fix.expected_effect: Checkout latency stays below SLA even when astronomy-db is delayed, preventing hidden-dependency cascades.

formula: penalty = 100 x (0.5 x impact + 0.3 x breadth + 0.2 x recovery); service score = 100 - worst penalty on that service; overall = mean of service scores weighted by the number of journeys the service sits on (at least 1; the larger of the map's count and the journeys it was seen to degrade). An experiment whose recovery was not measured (operator stop) contributes no recovery component.
methodology: An independent synthetic prober exercises four user journeys (home, product, cart, checkout) through the front proxy every second. It is the ground truth and does not depend on the application's own telemetry.

A baseline run fixes per-journey error rate and p95 latency and derives safety thresholds from them. A watchdog aborts any experiment that breaches a threshold or loses sight of the prober. Before injection, the safety agent reviews the plan against the baseline limits, recent outcomes and the learned limits, and may approve it, reduce its intensity or veto it; it can never raise an intensity. The planner remembers, across runs, the lowest intensity per target and fault kind that the watchdog or safety agent aborted, and does not propose that intensity or a higher one again within the lookback window. An advisory safety agent re-checks the live measurements every few seconds and may abort earlier; it can never cancel a watchdog abort, extend a fault or change a threshold.

Each experiment injects one fault (container crash, added network delay, packet loss or a traffic spike), measures every journey during the fault window (up to the abort for aborted runs), reverts the fault, and measures how long the journeys take to return inside the baseline band.

A declared combined failure injects 2 faults together as one experiment (one ledger entry per part, one watchdog, one safety review). Every journey limit is tightened for it: p95 limit x0.8, error-rate limit x0.8. It is scored once, as a whole.

Impact, breadth, recovery and the penalty are computed deterministically from those measurements. The hypothesis verdict compares the journeys the planner predicted would degrade with those that actually did: CONFIRMED when equal, PARTIAL when they overlap, REFUTED when they do not.
A hidden dependency is a journey that degraded by at least 0.3 although neither the hypothesis nor the dependency map expected it.

The analyst agent ranks weaknesses and the fixer agent proposes fixes from the measured results only; their output is validated against known experiments, services and an allowlist of compose keys. When Groq is unavailable or its output is invalid, rule-based fallbacks produce the same sections. Fixes are proposals; only restart-policy and raised memory or CPU limit fixes on one allowlisted service can be applied, by `faultline fix`, and are kept only if a re-run of the same experiment improves the penalty.
